_comment: The user's real homework. a = (1,2), b = (3,1), 'proj_a(b) = (b.a)a'.
Step 1 (b.a = 5) is CORRECT and is replayed as a component decomposition,
never as the perpendicular-foot picture -- in a projection problem that
foot IS the final answer, so the textbook rendering of a RIGHT step would
leak the answer (leak_guard names the downstream kind).
Step 2 forgets to divide by a.a, so 'scale a by 5' sends the arrow to
(5,10) -- 3.5x longer than the b it is supposed to be a shadow of.
Note what is NOT here: no correct_value of any kind. The scene cannot
leak an answer it was never given.

params.hint: a shadow can't be longer than the thing casting it
